title: Dooars river valleys for birders, by car
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

cost_split.item: Reserved car with driver, 6 days, half share
Best-grade forest corporation cottages and rooms, 5 nights with meals
Local guides for forest-edge and river walks
Chapramari watchtower safari, private jeep, half share

meta_description: 5 nights in the Dooars river valleys by car: Murti, Suntalekhola on the Neora Valley edge and Jhalong on the Jaldhaka, for birds, from ₹26,000 per person.
summary: Five slow nights for people who would rather watch a forktail than queue for a safari: one at Murti by the river, two at Suntalekhola's forest cottages on the edge of Neora Valley National Park, and two at Jhalong on the Jaldhaka, with Bindu and Paren. Your own car and the best government rooms. About ₹26,000 per person for two.
intro: The Dooars' rivers come out of the hills fast and clear, and their boulders and forest edges hold more birds than most safari tracks. This trip strings together three of the best spots: the Murti as it leaves the hills, the stream at Suntalekhola below Neora Valley National Park, and the Jaldhaka at Jhalong with Bhutan's forest across the water.

A car and driver let you be on the riverbank at first light and move on at midday. The best cottages at Suntalekhola and Jholung are simple but well placed, a few steps from the water. Because the valleys are not national parks, you can come in April, May and late September when the parks are quiet or closed, though river camps can shut after heavy rain. Check current status before you travel.
highlights: River birds on the Murti at dawn
Two nights at Suntalekhola's forest cottages
Walks along the Neora Valley forest edge
Jhalong and the Jaldhaka with Bhutan's hills opposite
Bindu barrage and the hill village of Paren

days.title: NJP to Murti
days.text: Your driver meets you at NJP or Bagdogra. Cross the Teesta at Sevoke, where the Coronation Bridge spans the gorge, and drive through Apalchand forest to Murti. Check into the best grade at the forest corporation's Murti Banani centre. In the late afternoon, take the Chapramari watchtower slot for gaur at the waterhole, or stay on the riverbed for wagtails, river lapwings and kingfishers as the light fades.

days.title: Dawn on the Murti, up to Suntalekhola
days.text: Be on the riverbed at first light, when birds are most active. After breakfast, drive up through the Chalsa tea gardens and Samsing to Suntalekhola. Cross the suspension footbridge to the forest corporation's cottages beside the stream that comes out of Neora Valley National Park. Spend the afternoon on the boulders: plumbeous and white-capped redstarts, forktails and wagtails work the water.

days.title: Forest edge walk and Rocky Island
days.text: Walk the forest edge above Suntalekhola early with a local guide, about ₹500–800, listening for barbets, bulbuls, drongos and, with luck, hornbills. Stay outside the national park unless you have permission. Late morning, drive down to Rocky Island, where the Murti runs between giant boulders, and walk the tea garden roads at Samsing. Back to the cottages for a quiet afternoon and evening.

days.title: Across to Jhalong
days.text: After a last morning by the stream, drive down to Chalsa and up the Jaldhaka valley to Jhalong. Check into the best grade at the forest corporation's Jholung River Camp. Spend the afternoon on the river road with binoculars, watching for river birds and raptors over the forest across the water in Bhutan. Dinner at the camp, and an early night.

days.title: Bindu and Paren
days.text: Drive up to Bindu, the last Indian village in the valley, where a barrage holds the Jaldhaka; carry ID, as this is the Bhutan border, with no crossing for travellers. Walk among cardamom and ginger plots with a local guide. Then climb to Paren for tea and the view, with forest birds along the road. Back to Jhalong for a late lunch and a final evening on the river.

days.title: Jhalong to NJP
days.text: One more dawn on the Jaldhaka, then breakfast and the drive down through Chalsa and Malbazar to Siliguri. Stop for tea at Chalsa. Reach NJP or Bagdogra by early afternoon. Leave a buffer of two to three hours before an evening flight or train, since highway traffic near Siliguri can be slow.

includes: Reserved car with driver for 6 days from NJP or Bagdogra and back
Five nights in best-grade forest corporation cottages and rooms, with meals
Local guides for three forest-edge or river walks
One Chapramari watchtower safari in a private jeep
excludes: Entry to Neora Valley National Park
save_money: Book the standard cottages or tents instead of the best grade; the river is the same.
Take shared jeeps from Chalsa to Samsing and Jhalong instead of keeping a car, if you do not mind waiting.
Skip the Chapramari safari and spend that evening on the Murti riverbed for free.
good_to_know: River camps can close after heavy rain and during the monsoon; check current status before you travel.
Gorumara and Chapramari close from about 16 June to 15 September; check current status before you travel.
Floods in October 2025 hit the Dooars rivers; ask about road and camp damage before booking.
Carry ID at Bindu near the Bhutan border.

faqs.q: Is the Dooars good for birdwatching?
faqs.a: Yes. Rivers coming out of the hills, forest edges, tea gardens and grassland give a wide range of species in a small area. River birds such as redstarts, forktails and wagtails are easy to see on boulders. Winter brings more species. Bring binoculars and a field guide.

faqs.q: Why stay at Suntalekhola for two nights?
faqs.a: Because birds are most active at dawn, and a second night gives you two dawns by the stream and a full day for forest-edge walks and Rocky Island. The forest corporation's cottages sit just across the hanging bridge, so you are on the water within minutes of waking.

faqs.q: Can we enter Neora Valley National Park?
faqs.a: Not on this plan. Suntalekhola and Samsing sit on the park's southern edge. Entry needs a forest permit and is more commonly arranged from the Lava side in Kalimpong district. Walk with a guide on the forest edge, and do not enter the park without permission.

Local guides are available at Samsing, Suntalekhola and Jhalong for forest-edge and river walks, at about ₹500–800 a day, indicative. Not all are specialist birders, so ask your lodge for someone who knows bird calls. Experienced birders may prefer to go with their own field guide.

faqs.q: Can we do this trip in the off-season?
faqs.a: Yes, more easily than the park trips. April, May and late September work in the valleys, with fewer visitors. Avoid the heaviest monsoon from June to August, when rivers rise, roads wash out and camps may close. Check current status before you travel.

The best grades at Murti Banani, Suntaleykhola and Jholung River Camp have attached bathrooms and simple furniture. They are not resorts. Power backup and hot water can be limited. The setting, a few steps from the water, is the reason to come.

faqs.q: Is this a good trip for a couple?
faqs.a: Yes, for couples who like quiet. Days are slow, evenings are early and there are few other visitors in the valleys outside weekends. The car gives you privacy and flexibility. It suits a relaxed honeymoon better than a packed sightseeing one.

faqs.q: What camera gear should we bring?
faqs.a: A long lens, 300 mm or more, for birds on the river; binoculars; spare batteries and a power bank, since charging can be unreliable; and a rain cover. Camera fees apply in the parks. Keep gear dry when crossing streams.

faqs.q: Can we add a rhino safari?
faqs.a: Yes. Add a night at Lataguri for Gorumara's watchtowers, which are about an hour from Murti and Samsing. Book slots online early, and remember Gorumara closes from about mid-June to mid-September.
